title: Adobe's emergency patch, SAP trust failures and browser theft
overview: Adobe has patched the actively exploited Commerce and Magento flaw, while N-able adds an account check for N-central administrators. New SAP and Siemens vulnerabilities threaten trusted infrastructure, browser campaigns abuse Google-hosted content, and an exposed passenger database holds 220 million records.
paragraphs: [cheerful] Good morning, it's 5:22 AM. Tuesday, the eighth of September, twenty twenty-six. five twenty-two AM is brought to you by Lab five twenty-two, a technology partner for mid-market businesses, providing cyber security services and enterprise operational software. Email us at hello at lab five twenty-two dot co dot uk if you think we can help your business. [short pause]

[serious] Adobe's emergency patch has arrived. Monday's release addresses the Commerce and Magento zero-day we were waiting on yesterday, and the newly disclosed mechanism is template injection: attacker-controlled content becomes code running as the application user. CVE-2026-75650 scores ten, reachable over the network with no login and no click. [short pause] The attacks now described include a Rust backdoor and a P-H-P web shell. That's persistence to investigate, not just a vulnerable package to replace.

[calm] For Adobe Commerce, affected releases include the 2 point 4 point 4 through 2 point 4 point 9 branches at their August twenty twenty-six patch levels and earlier. Magento Open Source has the same cutoff across 2 point 4 point 6 through 2 point 4 point 9, and Commerce B-to-B releases are affected too. Apply Monday's vendor patch for your branch; the fixed build numbers haven't been named here. [confident] I'd give that an emergency change slot, with compromise checks alongside it rather than after the ticket's closed.

[short pause] And there's a useful addition to yesterday's N-central response: N-able is advising administrators to look for newly created accounts they don't recognise. N-central is trusted to administer other machines, so an unexplained account there deserves investigation into what it accessed or changed. [serious] Make that an explicit check in the incident work, not an assumption that the hotfix tidied everything up.

[curious] From trusted administration to a rather dubious verification: Cisco Talos began investigating ClearFake after seeing a D-L-L named “verification dot google” executing from WebDAV at a Ukrainian government organisation. The infection chain delivers Amatera stealer, ZigCryptoStealer and NetSupport Manager, a remote-control tool. [short pause] For detection teams, that gives you something concrete to hunt: D-L-L execution from WebDAV and those payloads. A reassuring filename isn't a signature.

And the browser itself is becoming the delivery surface. Another campaign tracked by Talos abuses the Google Visualization A-P-I to fetch obfuscated JavaScript from a publicly published Google Sheets document and inject it into the victim's browser session for cryptocurrency theft. [serious] Here, Google's infrastructure is carrying command-and-control content, not vouching for it. If you're investigating browser-based theft, inspect what those requests returned; a familiar destination alone won't clear them.

[short pause] Staying in the browser, researchers have also described PEEP, a Chromium post-exploitation toolkit disguised as a bookmarks extension that supports host command execution. The distinction matters: it's for use after compromise, not evidence of a fresh Chrome or Edge entry-point flaw. [calm] In an incident, an apparently mundane extension deserves scrutiny if browser activity coincides with unexpected host commands.

[long pause] Now to the new infrastructure flaws, and S-A-P has two that worry me for different reasons. NetWeaver Message Server coordinates application-server components. CVE-2026-58240 lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access register an unauthorised component because the service doesn't sufficiently verify who's joining. No click required; nine point eight. [serious] The attacker can pass themselves off as part of the application environment and potentially perform unauthorised actions inside it. A membership check is doing the work of a security boundary, and it isn't checking enough.

[calm] Versions 9 point 18, 9 point 19 and 9 point 20 are affected. Check the S-A-P advisory and restrict service reachability to the application-server systems that need it. [short pause] Alongside that, CVE-2026-44756 scores ten in the Extended Passport Protocol processing library, which handles tracing context passed between S-A-P components. A malformed header in a network request can trigger memory-safety failure without a login or user interaction. Abnormal termination is described; don't turn the score alone into a claim of confirmed code execution.

For that library, the affected releases are 7 point 22 EXT, 7 point 53, 8 point 04, and 9 point 18 through 9 point 20. No fixed builds have been specified for either S-A-P flaw. [confident] Establish which deployed components use the library and get the remediation instructions from S-A-P, rather than treating it as one standalone service to find.

[short pause] In operational technology, Siemens Reyrolle 7SR5 protection relays have a particularly uncomfortable web-interface flaw. These devices sit in electrical protection systems. CVE-2026-62645 exposes information that lets an attacker calculate current and past session identifiers, bypass authentication and gain unauthorised device access. [serious] Nine point eight, over the network, no login or click. Session identifiers shouldn't be a maths exercise. [calm] Versions before V2 point 70 are affected; move to V2 point 70 or later and keep the web interface reachable only from authorised management networks.

And for enterprise Java estates, Hitachi's Cosminexus Component Container has unauthenticated network-reachable deserialisation of untrusted data, scoring nine point eight. CVE-2026-71374 affects numerous release lines. Fixed boundaries include 11-70-03, 11-60-03 and 11-20-10; older branches have their own cutoffs, and some have no safe release specified. [calm] Check Hitachi's branch-specific guidance before choosing an upgrade. The important bit is that this application-server component can process hostile serialised data without a login or a click.

[short pause] One more device update: another public exploit affects D-Link DIR-822A firmware A underscore 101, this time an out-of-bounds write in its L-two-T-P control-message parser. It requires a low-privilege login over the network. D-Link haven't identified safe firmware, so restrict untrusted reachability and check their guidance; public code isn't confirmation of active attacks.

[long pause] Finally, an exposed Vietnam-linked Advance Passenger Information System database held two hundred and twenty million passenger and crew records, spanning twenty seventeen to twenty twenty-six. Names, passport numbers, dates of birth, nationalities and flight details were included. [serious] That's records, not a confirmed count of unique people. These systems hold advance traveller information for border processing, and the combination makes convincing travel-themed fraud a real concern. For teams operating passenger-data integrations, check database exposure and access logs; no particular software flaw has been identified as the cause.

[confident] I'd put Adobe's emergency change and the accompanying compromise investigation first today. Then I'd establish who can reach those S-A-P services and Siemens web interfaces, while keeping the newly created N-central accounts check in the response work. [cheerful] five twenty-two AM, brought to you by Lab five twenty-two. Find us at lab five twenty-two dot co dot uk.
